text: The selflessness of dharmas is apprehended by the self that is imagined in relation to the apprehender and the apprehended, etc., in the case of those who, in their youth, conceive of the nature of dharmas as having a self. It is not the selflessness of the self that is not posited, which is the object of the Buddhas. Similarly, even for mere designation, the entry into selflessness occurs through the self imagined in relation to other designations, and thus, through the establishment of mere designation, the entry into the selflessness of all dharmas takes place; it does not arise from the negation of their existence.
